subject: Civil Engineering
title: Corrosion of Reinforcement
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Corrosion of Reinforcement.

hook.text: Salt from winter roads seeps into bridge decks. The rebar inside rusts and expands.

buildup.text: Rust occupies six times more volume than steel — it cracks the concrete from inside out.

discovery.text: Carbonation lowers concrete's pH over decades — losing the alkaline shield that protects steel.

twist.text: Chlorides from seawater or deicing salts attack even before carbonation reaches the rebar.

climax.text: Epoxy-coated and stainless-steel rebar resist corrosion — but cost significantly more.

punchline.text: Concrete's worst enemy hides inside it — rusting steel that blows it apart.

quiz.question: How does rebar corrosion damage concrete?
options: Rust weakens the steel until it snaps under load
Rust expands to six times the steel's volume, cracking the surrounding concrete
Corroding steel releases heat that melts the cement paste

details.summary: Reinforcement corrosion occurs when chlorides from deicing salt or seawater, or carbonation from atmospheric CO2, destroy the protective alkaline environment around embedded steel. Corroding steel expands to several times its original volume, cracking and spalling the concrete cover from within.
details.whyItMatters: Reinforcement corrosion is the leading cause of concrete structure deterioration worldwide, costing hundreds of billions of dollars annually in repair and replacement globally.
takeaways: Chloride penetration and carbonation are the two main corrosion mechanisms
Corroding rebar expands up to six times its volume, cracking concrete from within
Corrosion damage typically becomes visible 15 to 25 years after initiation

faq.question: How does chloride cause reinforcement corrosion in concrete?
faq.answer: Chloride ions from deicing salt or seawater penetrate through concrete pores to the rebar surface. When chloride concentration exceeds a threshold (about 0.4% by weight of cement), it breaks down the passive oxide film protecting the steel.

faq.question: What methods prevent or slow reinforcement corrosion?
faq.answer: Low permeability concrete with adequate cover is the primary defense. Additional measures include epoxy-coated or stainless steel rebar, corrosion inhibitor admixtures, surface sealers, and cathodic protection systems that use electrical current to prevent the corrosion reaction from occurring.
